name: Halls Creek
reason: Town a visitor source gives its own page and that visitors base in: Wikivoyage Kimberley lists it as the gateway to Wolfe Creek Crater; Australia's North West has a Halls Creek page naming China Wall, Old Halls Creek, Caroline Pool, Sawpit Gorge and Palm Springs around it (rule 1, two counted sources; rule 2).
objection: Little in the town itself; its draws are the crater, the Bungle Bungles and small sites around it, so the proposer must not list it as a wrapper beside its own attractions.

name: Fitzroy Crossing
reason: Base town with its own Australia's North West page (base for Geikie Gorge, Tunnel Creek and Windjana; Crossing Inn of 1897, old crossing, art galleries in the visitor centre) and a Wikivoyage Kimberley Towns entry (rule 1, two counted sources).
objection: Its headline draw, Danggu Geikie Gorge, is a separate national park; the town itself is a service stop with a few heritage remnants.

name: Beagle Bay
reason: Duplicate of Sacred Heart Church, Beagle Bay: the only thing any visitor source names here is the church (Wikivoyage Kimberley), so the community is a wrapper around its own attraction (COVERAGE: a town is a spot only when the town itself is a draw).
objection: Visit Broome lists Beagle Bay among the four Dampier Peninsula communities visitors pass through; if the church were dropped the community would be the place to name.

name: Lombadina
reason: Re-looked for a counted source: Lombadina's own site invites visitors (day pass $10 per vehicle; craft shop, bush-timber church and beach open weekdays 8am-4pm; mud-crabbing, kayak and whale-watching tours), and a Lonely Planet Dampier Peninsula article (search snippet; the URL now redirects) names its Aboriginal-led tours. Visit Broome names it as one of the four peninsula communities.
objection: Only one counted source and that one not readable now; the community's own site is an operator page; a visit is on community terms with seasonal weekend closures, and the beach and church are modest.

name: Kalumburu
reason: Wikivoyage Gibb River Road names it as the end of the 208 km Kalumburu Road, and Visit Broome's Gibb River Road page gives it a section (two counted sources); a remote mission community with beaches and fishing (Honeymoon Bay, McGowans Island).
objection: Neither source names something to see in the community itself, only the two permits needed to enter; access is at the Traditional Owners' discretion and may be closed. The candidate note is wrong: Mitchell Falls is reached from a turn-off on Kalumburu Road, not from Kalumburu.

name: Imintji
reason: A service stop (campground and community store) rather than a draw: Wikivoyage Gibb River Road lists an art centre, camping and store; Visit Broome says the store is not open in 2026, so no fuel. Fails rule 2 (a business/services stop) and rule 3 (its visitors are there for Bell Gorge).
objection: The Imintji art centre could be a short cultural stop; if a visitor source confirms it is open, it might reach review.

name: Cape Leveque
reason: Headland at the tip of the Dampier Peninsula, named by Wikivoyage Broome (Go next) and Lonely Planet (POI 'Cape Leveque (Kooljaman)'); a well-known Kimberley beach and red-cliff destination (rule 1).
objection: Kooljaman, the resort that held the visitor access, closed indefinitely on 1 Nov 2021 and no reopening was found; an operator says Cape Leveque point is closed indefinitely and access is limited (rule 2: open to the public is unconfirmed).

name: Sacred Heart Church, Beagle Bay
reason: A church a visitor source singles out for its interior: Wikivoyage Kimberley lists it under Other destinations, a hand-built church whose mother-of-pearl altar fuses Indigenous and Catholic art (rule 2: an interior visitors go in for).
objection: One counted source; a 20-30 minute stop 120 km up the peninsula, on community land.

name: Buccaneer Archipelago
reason: Island group named by Visit Broome (Derby: 'the islands of the Buccaneer Archipelago') and Wikivoyage Broome (boat trips reach it), and inside DBCA's Lalang-gaddam Marine Park; it is the place the Derby and Broome cruises go to.
objection: Visitors go for Horizontal Falls, a candidate of its own inside the archipelago; the archipelago as a whole is an area seen only from boats and planes, so it risks being a near-duplicate wrapper of Horizontal Falls.

name: Horizontal Falls
reason: Headline draw named by Tourism WA (its own destination page in the Kimberley menu), Australia's North West (homepage feature 'Garaan-ngaddim Horizontal Falls'), DBCA (Lalang-gaddam Marine Park, 'awe-inspiring') and Wikivoyage Kimberley (rule 1, several counted sources). The place the seaplane and boat tours go is the spot (A spot is a place).
objection: Reachable only by paid flight or boat tour; it is inside the Buccaneer Archipelago (keep it as the one spot and fold the archipelago in, not both).

name: Eighty Mile Beach
reason: Re-looked and found a counted source: DBCA's Eighty Mile Beach Marine Park page (220 km beach for fishing, shell-combing, sunsets, Ramsar shorebirds, flatback turtles Oct-Feb; caravan park access). A long linear feature pinned at its main access point (Eighty Mile Beach Caravan Park).
objection: Only one counted source and very remote; its access points (Eighty Mile Beach Caravan Park, Cape Keraudren) may lie on the Pilbara boundary: confirm which region holds the main access point.

name: James Price Point
reason: Re-looked for a counted source and found none: only science news on the Walmadany dinosaur tracks and a Q&A travel blog that says there are no tourist facilities; the tracks are intertidal and visible only at low tide (rule 1 fails).
objection: Internationally known dinosaur trackways and a red-cliff coast 60 km north of Broome; a Goolarabooloo-guided tour or a Tourism WA page, if found, would make it a review.

name: Montgomery Reef
reason: Re-looked and found a counted source: DBCA's Lalang-gaddam Marine Park page names Yowjab (Montgomery Reef) as one of the park's two awe-inspiring sights, and features it in its gallery; it is the place the Kimberley coast cruises and flights go (A spot is a place).
objection: One counted source; seen only from a cruise or scenic flight, and it lies in the same marine park as Horizontal Falls.

name: Mornington Wilderness Camp
reason: Closed: Wikivoyage Gibb River Road says 'Mornington Camp has closed down' (rule 2), and it is an operator's camp rather than a place.
objection: AWC still manages the Mornington sanctuary; if visitor access reopens it would be judged as a wildlife sanctuary.

name: Cape Londonderry
reason: Re-looked for a counted source and found none: it appears only in a cruise operator's helicopter-flight brochure; no road access and nothing a visitor can do there (rules 1 and 2).
objection: It is WA's northernmost mainland point, a geographic superlative some flights mention.

name: Canning Stock Route
reason: A 1,850 km historic 4WD route that Australia's North West's Halls Creek page names among the outback drives from Halls Creek and that Wikivoyage Kimberley mentions as a 'full-on expedition' (rule 1 met once).
objection: A route, not a place you stop at for half an hour; Wikivoyage calls it beyond its scope; most of its length and its southern trailhead (Wiluna) lie outside the Kimberley (probably wa-golden-outback / Pilbara), so the proposer must decide one region and pin it at the midpoint; permits needed.

name: Cable Beach
reason: Broome's headline sight: Wikivoyage Broome ('what Broome is famous for', 22 km of white sand, camel rides), Australia's North West homepage feature, Visit Broome (rule 1, three counted sources).
objection: None of substance; only a low page-view count because the article title is disambiguated.

name: Gantheaume Point
reason: Wikivoyage Broome See listing: red rock formations against blue sea and dinosaur footprints (concrete replicas at the sign, real prints beyond the jetty at the lowest tides) (rules 1-3).
objection: One counted source here; the real footprints are only seen at extreme low tide, so most visitors see rocks and replicas.

name: Town Beach, Broome
reason: Wikivoyage Broome names it as Broome's favourite Staircase to the Moon viewing spot and the access to the WWII flying-boat wrecks at very low tide; Visit Broome lists Town Beach among Broome's areas and has a Catalina wrecks page (rule 1, two counted sources).
objection: A small sheltered town beach; its two draws (the moon effect, the wrecks) are tide- and season-dependent.

name: Reddell Beach
reason: Wikivoyage Broome names it: the quiet south-west-facing beach between Gantheaume Point and Kabbarli Lookout (rule 1, one source).
objection: One passing sentence and nothing to do beyond a quiet beach; close to Gantheaume Point, so it may be a near-duplicate of that stop.

name: Kabbarli Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage Broome See listing: scenic red rocks at Entrance Point where ships turn into Roebuck Bay (rule 1, one source).
objection: One source, which also calls the approach grubby through the port industrial area; a short look, similar red rocks to Gantheaume Point nearby.

name: Roebuck Bay
reason: An area, not a stop: visitors reach the bay at Broome Bird Observatory and Town Beach, both candidates of their own, so the bay is a near-duplicate of them (rule 3). Wikivoyage Broome names it only in passing.
objection: Ramsar-listed shorebird habitat of international importance; if the proposer wants one spot for the bay, it should be the Bird Observatory.

name: Broome Bird Observatory
reason: Wikivoyage Broome Do listing: 300 species, the Roebuck Bay migratory waders, hours (Apr-Oct 8am-4pm), entry fee and camping (rules 1, 2 and 4: a seasonal venue is fine).
objection: One counted source; dirt access road; seasonal opening.

name: Japanese Cemetery, Broome
reason: Wikivoyage Broome See listing: 900 Japanese pearl divers plus Chinese, Malay and Afghan sections, open daily 7am-8pm; a heritage site that tells Broome's pearling story, not a minor plaque (rules 1-3).
objection: One counted source; a 20-30 minute stop; a cemetery could be read as a minor memorial.

name: Broome Historical Museum
reason: Wikivoyage Broome See listing: pearling and the 1942 Japanese air raid, open daily, paid entry (rules 1-2).
objection: One counted source; a small volunteer local-history museum with short hours (10am-1pm).

name: Pearl Luggers
reason: Wikivoyage Broome See listing: two restored pearl luggers beside a showroom, seen on a 90-minute guided tour ($30) on the pearling industry (rule 2: a tour of heritage vessels).
objection: It is Willie Creek's pearl showroom: a shop with an attached tour (brief: shops and operators are rejected); one counted source.

name: Willie Creek Pearl Farm
reason: A place, not just an operator: a working pearl farm 38 km north of Broome whose tour shows the nursery, the creek and harvesting; named by Wikivoyage Broome (See) and Visit Broome (rule 1, two counted sources; rule 2).
objection: Visited only on the operator's paid tour; 4WD access road; open Mar-Dec.

name: Short Street Gallery
reason: A commercial gallery selling art (Wikivoyage Broome: 'for sale'), i.e. a shop (rule 2).
objection: Shows contemporary Aboriginal art from the Kimberley and Pilbara that visitors may browse.

name: Broome Fruit Bat Roost
reason: Wikivoyage Broome names it: thousands of fruit bats rise at dusk from the roost at the end of Short Street (rule 1, one source).
objection: One sentence in one source, a dusk-only spectacle with no defined site, and a short look; may be too minor.

name: Malcolm Douglas Crocodile Park
reason: Wikivoyage Broome See listing: a wildlife park with several crocodile species, birds and other fauna, daily 2-5pm, 3pm feeding, paid entry (rules 1-2).
objection: One counted source; short afternoon opening hours.

name: SSJG Heritage Centre
reason: Wikivoyage Broome See listing: exhibits on the Sisters of St John of God's work among Aboriginal people (rule 1, one source).
objection: Opens only weekday mornings Feb-Nov, by donation, a small single-room exhibit; one source.

name: Staircase to the Moon
reason: Duplicate of Town Beach, Broome: a seasonal phenomenon whose place is Town Beach (Wikivoyage Broome: 'the favourite viewing spot is Town Beach'); keep it as one by putting the phenomenon and its dry-season full-moon dates in Town Beach's bio (brief: a seasonal phenomenon is kept as its place).
objection: Tourism WA and Visit Broome both feature it prominently; it is a headline Broome experience, so it must not be lost when merged.

name: Shinju Matsuri
reason: A festival held the last two weeks of August (rule 4).
objection: None: a recurring event belongs in the destination's text.

name: Broome Turf Club
reason: A racecourse with races only May-August (rule 4: a recurring event venue, not a place to visit when you arrive).
objection: Racing carnival is a social highlight in season; mention in timing text.

name: Boab Prison Tree, Derby
reason: Derby's best-known sight: Wikivoyage Derby See listing (1,500-year-old hollow boab, 14.7 m girth) and Visit Broome's Derby page (rule 1, two counted sources).
objection: A short stop; Wikivoyage notes the prison legend is a myth (the tree was an ossuary), so the bio must not repeat it as fact.

name: Derby Jetty
reason: Wikivoyage Derby See listing: the 1960s horseshoe jetty for fishing and sunset, with a tidal range up to 12 m; Visit Broome's Derby page leads on those tides (rules 1-3; a harbour stop a guide names).
objection: Essentially one counted source for the jetty itself; a short sunset/fishing stop.

name: Frosty's Pool
reason: Wikivoyage Derby See listing: a rusting 1944 swimming pool built by soldiers by the highway at the Boab turn-off (a quirky roadside curiosity).
objection: One sentence in one source; a ten-minute look; probably only worth it alongside the Boab Prison Tree.

name: Mowanjum Culture Centre
reason: Wikivoyage Derby See listing (Worrorra, Ngarinyin and Wunambal art, crafts and museum; hours; $5) and Visit Broome's Derby page (Mowanjum Art and Culture Centre) (rule 1, two counted sources; rule 2).
objection: Partly an art sales outlet; closed Sundays and Mondays.

name: Norval Gallery
reason: Temporarily closed per Wikivoyage Derby, and a commercial gallery selling art (rule 2).
objection: Could be reconsidered if it reopens.

name: Wharfinger's House Museum
reason: Wikivoyage Derby See listing (local history museum in the wharfinger's stilted bungalow) and Visit Broome's Derby page (Wharfinger House Museum, aviation history) (rule 1, two counted sources).
objection: Small; entry by key from the visitor centre during its hours.

name: One Mile Dinner Camp
reason: A picnic spot at the end of the golf course, a local reserve used at sundown (Leave out: local parks and reserves; rule 3, minor historic site).
objection: Wikivoyage Derby names it with a drovers' history.

name: Derby Speedway
reason: A motorsport venue with races May-October (rule 4: recurring events).
objection: None.

name: Mud Crab Races, Derby
reason: An event held two or three times a year (rule 4).
objection: None.

name: Derby Sportsmen's Club
reason: A golf club, a local sports amenity (rule 2).
objection: None.

name: Derby Memorial Swimming Pool
reason: A local public pool, an amenity rather than a visitor draw (rule 2; Leave out).
objection: None.

name: Gibb River Road
reason: Named by Wikivoyage (its own itinerary article: 'a bucket-list Australian adventure'), Australia's North West homepage ('The Legendary Outback Drive') and Visit Broome (its own page) (rule 1, three counted sources): the drive is the attraction for many visitors.
objection: A road is the way you get there, and its places (Windjana, Tunnel Creek, Bell, Galvans, Manning, Emma gorges, El Questro) are spots of their own (A spot is a place); the owner should decide whether a 647 km 4WD route is a spot, pinned at its midpoint.

name: Windjana Gorge
reason: DBCA park page for Bandilngan (Windjana Gorge) National Park (3.5 km gorge through a Devonian reef, walking trails, fossils, freshwater crocodiles, open May-Nov), Wikivoyage Kimberley and Visit Broome (rule 1, three counted sources).
objection: The candidate is the gorge rather than the park; they are the same place, so keep one entry (the gorge is what the park is).

name: Tunnel Creek
reason: DBCA page for Dimalurru (Tunnel Creek) National Park: a 750 m walk through a limestone tunnel with bats, crocodiles and Jandamarra history; also Visit Broome and Australia's North West (rule 1, three counted sources).
objection: Dry-season 4WD access only; closed in the wet (a seasonal venue is fine).

name: Bell Gorge
reason: DBCA site page Dalmanyi (Bell Gorge): a waterfall and deep swimming pool reached by a 2 km walk; Australia's North West listing and Visit Broome ('one of the Gibb's most spectacular gorges') (rule 1, three counted sources).
objection: Dry-season 4WD access only. The candidate note is wrong on location: the car park is 30 km off the road via Silent Grove Road, not 1 km from Imintji; pin from DBCA.

name: Manning Gorge
reason: Wikivoyage Gibb River Road (swimming gorge 10 km north of Mount Barnett) and Visit Broome (its own section: walk, campground, day passes) (rule 1, two counted sources).
objection: Private station land with a day-use fee paid at the roadhouse; dry season only.

name: Adcock Gorge
reason: Wikivoyage Gibb River Road names it as a scenic spot 4 km south of the road (rule 1, one source).
objection: One passing line; no second counted source found (Visit Broome and DBCA do not list it); a lesser gorge beside better-known ones.

name: Galvans Gorge
reason: Wikivoyage Gibb River Road and Visit Broome ('a beautiful little gorge with easy access ... a delightful spot for a refreshing swim', in Wunaamin Conservation Park) (rule 1, two counted sources).
objection: A small gorge and short visit.

name: Wunnamurra Gorge
reason: Wikivoyage Gibb River Road names it near Mount Elizabeth Station (rule 1, one source).
objection: A bare mention with no description; on a private cattle station reached through it; a marginal place needs two sources.

name: Warla Gorge
reason: Wikivoyage Gibb River Road names it near Mount Elizabeth Station (rule 1, one source).
objection: A bare mention with no description; on a private cattle station; a marginal place needs two sources.

name: Emma Gorge
reason: Tourism WA attraction page (a gorge with a pool fed by a waterfall and a thermal spring, about 50 minutes from Kununurra), Wikivoyage Gibb River Road and Visit Broome (rule 1, three counted sources).
objection: Inside El Questro Wilderness Park (needs its permit); keep as a distinct site within the park, not a duplicate of it.

name: Zebedee Springs
reason: Re-looked and found a counted source: Tourism WA's Zebedee Springs attraction page (thermal pools in a palm forest, 1.5 km return walk, public access mornings May-Sept); Visit Broome's Gibb River Road page also pictures it (rules 1-2).
objection: Inside El Questro; mornings only for the public, afternoons reserved for Homestead guests; seasonal.

name: Queen Victoria's Head
reason: Wikivoyage Gibb River Road names it as a prominent rock 6 km past the Lennard River crossing (a roadside landform a guide names).
objection: One line in one source; a look from the road, not a half-hour stop.

name: China Wall
reason: Rule 1 and 2: counted sources found on re-look: Tourism WA attraction page (westernaustralia.com/au/attraction/china-wall) and Australia's North West listing (australiasnorthwest.com/listing/china-wall/162, fetched) name it as a stop near Halls Creek; a quartz vein wall with a short walk, photos and a creek picnic spot; a classic quirky roadside landmark.
objection: Short stop (often 20-30 min) on a pastoral-lease access road off Duncan Road; candidate had no coordinates yet, the pin must come from resolve-pin.

name: Ivanhoe Crossing
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Kununurra 'Further out' listing and Australia's North West Kununurra guide (fetched) both name it; rule 2: causeway on the Ord where visitors fish, picnic and watch the river; a named local icon.
objection: Mostly a fishing and photo stop on a submerged causeway; no swimming (crocodiles) and impassable after rain.

name: Mitchell Plateau
reason: Rule 3: duplicate of Mitchell River National Park / Mitchell Falls. The plateau is the park's area; Wikivoyage only names it as the destination of Kalumburu Road, and sources name the falls and park as the place visitors go.
objection: Australia's North West uses 'Mitchell Plateau' as a section heading; the proposer could use the name for the park spot if preferred, but it should not be a second spot.

name: Mitchell Falls
reason: Rule 1: obvious Kimberley headline draw; Wikivoyage Wyndham listing, DBCA Mitchell River National Park page (fetched: 'Mitchell Falls must be the natural highlight', walk from Mitchell Falls Campground) and Australia's North West Gibb River Road page; rule 2: a half-day walk to a four-tiered waterfall.
objection: Remote: 4WD on Kalumburu Road plus an Uunguu Visitor Pass, dry season only; overlaps Mitchell River National Park (proposer should keep both only if the park offers more than the falls).

name: King George Falls
reason: Rule 1: Australia's North West page (fetched), Tourism WA attraction page, DBCA site page and Wikivoyage Wyndham all name it; WA's highest twin falls, a headline Kimberley coast sight. The boat or flight is the way in, the falls are the spot.
objection: Reachable only by expedition cruise, Faraway Bay boat or scenic flight; flow is strongest Apr-May; few independent travellers reach it.

name: Mitchell River National Park
reason: Rule 1 re-look: DBCA Explore Parks page for Mitchell River National Park (fetched) is a counted source, with campground, trails, rock art, Little Mertens Falls and Mitchell Falls; rule 2: a multi-day park visit.
objection: Near-duplicate risk with Mitchell Falls: the falls are the reason most visitors come; if only one goes in, prefer Mitchell Falls.

name: Drysdale River National Park
reason: Rule 2: DBCA page (fetched) says there is no vehicle access and no infrastructure, entry by permit only (not issued Jan-May), best seen from a scenic flight; a rarely visited wilderness that a visitor cannot simply go to (COVERAGE: rarely visited places fail).
objection: DBCA does have a visitor page and lists Morgan and Solea Falls; a self-sufficient permitted bushwalker can visit, so the owner may want it as a standalone wilderness spot.

name: Echidna Chasm
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Purnululu See listing (fetched) and DBCA Purnululu page (fetched) both name it as a highlight of the northern Bungle Bungles; rule 2: 2 km return walk into a 200 m deep, metre-wide palm-lined chasm.
objection: Inside Purnululu National Park; must be distinct from the Bungle Bungle Range spot (it is: a separate trail from Bloodwoods car park).

name: Mini Palms Gorge
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Purnululu and DBCA Purnululu page (both fetched) name it among the northern highlights; rule 2: a 4.4 km return trail to viewing platforms over a palm-filled gorge.
objection: Second-tier compared with Echidna Chasm and Cathedral Gorge; a challenging scramble that many visitors skip.

name: Cathedral Gorge
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Purnululu and DBCA Purnululu (both fetched) single it out as the awe-inspiring amphitheatre of the southern Bungle Bungles; rule 2: 2 km return walk; one of the park's two signature walks.
objection: Inside Purnululu National Park; distinctness from a Bungle Bungle Range spot depends on how that spot is defined (it should be the domes/range, not this gorge).

name: The Domes
reason: Rule 1 met (Wikivoyage Purnululu and DBCA's 'The Domes' 1.4 km walk, both fetched), but rule 3 is doubtful: the beehive domes ARE the Bungle Bungle Range most visitors mean, so this is likely a near-duplicate of a Bungle Bungle Range spot.
objection: For keep: DBCA lists the Domes Walk as its own trail and it is where visitors see the iconic beehives up close; if the range itself is listed as the park or a broad area, this walk may deserve its own spot.

name: The Window
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Purnululu (fetched) names it, 2 km from Piccaninny car park, dramatic at sunset; one counted source only.
objection: Rule 3: it is a point along the Piccaninny Creek bed route (the same walk as Piccaninny Creek Lookout and Whip Snake Gorge); DBCA does not give it its own heading. Likely better folded into one Piccaninny Gorge/Creek spot.

name: Whip Snake Gorge
reason: Rule 3: part of a larger route: a side canyon reached by continuing past The Window, a 10 km return extension of the Piccaninny Creek walk; one Wikivoyage line, no separate DBCA entry.
objection: A genuine named side gorge that experienced hikers seek out; could be mentioned in a Piccaninny Gorge spot's bio.

name: Piccaninny Creek Lookout
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Purnululu and DBCA (fetched: 'Creek Lookout Trail within Piccaninny Gorge, 2.8 km return', views over the creek and domes) both name it.
objection: Rule 3: it branches off the Cathedral Gorge trail and shares the Piccaninny car park with The Domes, Cathedral Gorge and The Window; may be best as one Piccaninny Creek spot rather than a separate lookout.

name: Kungkalanayi Lookout
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Purnululu (500 m walk, 360-degree panorama of the Bungle Bungles, aflame at sunset) and DBCA Purnululu page (fetched, own heading); rule 2: the park's sunset viewpoint with its own car park.
objection: Short visit (about 30 min) and flagged part-of-signal; it is on the access road rather than a trail the app lists, so it stands as its own lookout.

name: Osmand Lookout
reason: Rule 3: a minor lookout on the Bloodwoods/Escarpment trail beside Echidna Chasm; Wikivoyage gives one line and DBCA only names it as a destination from the Echidna car park, not a draw in itself.
objection: It is a real 1 km hike with views over the northern range; could be mentioned in Echidna Chasm's bio.

name: Piccaninny Crater
reason: Rule 2: Wikivoyage Purnululu says it 'can really only be seen from the air'; eroded beyond recognition on the ground, with no visitor access or trail, so a visitor cannot go and see it.
objection: Notable meteorite crater with a Wikipedia article and 1,198 views; scenic flights over Purnululu may point it out.

name: Lake Kununurra
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Kununurra See listing and Australia's North West Kununurra guide ('Ord River & Lake Kununurra', sunset cruises; both fetched); rule 2: drowned forest, picnic and swimming spots, cruises and birdlife.
objection: Overlaps the Ord River cruise and Lily Creek Lagoon (a side-arm); the lake, not the cruise, is the spot.

name: Diversion Dam
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Kununurra only (fetched): dam with gates and machinery, shady picnic area, boat ramp and fishing; one counted source and a short stop.
objection: Rule 3: it is the downstream end of Lake Kununurra and carries the highway; a picnic/fishing pull-out more for locals than visitors; Australia's North West does not single it out.

name: Elephant Rock
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Kununurra (fetched) lists it, and Australia's North West's Lily Creek Lagoon listing names 'the iconic Sleeping Buddha/Elephant Rock' as the view; a recognisable local landmark.
objection: Mostly seen from Lily Creek Lagoon or the highway; Wikivoyage says the climb is rough, unmarked and underwhelming, so it may be a view rather than a place to go (near-duplicate of Lily Creek Lagoon).

name: Kelly's Knob
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Kununurra and Australia's North West ('a trip to Kelly's Knob is a must', sunrise and sunset; both fetched); rule 2: hilltop lookout with a trail to the summit over Kununurra and the Ord irrigation area.
objection: A short drive-up lookout; a 30-minute visit at most.

name: Celebrity Tree Park
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Kununurra only (fetched): a free 24-hour park where stars of the film Australia planted trees; quirky story, one counted source.
objection: Wikivoyage itself says several trees have died and plaques have dropped off, so there is little to see; arguably an ordinary town park (negative benchmark) and the venue of the Ord Valley Muster.

name: Lily Creek Lagoon
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Kununurra and Australia's North West Kununurra guide (own listing: wetlands, birdlife, views of Elephant Rock; both fetched) - two counted sources.
objection: Rule 3: a side-arm of Lake Kununurra, so a near-duplicate if Lake Kununurra is kept; a short waterside stop in town.

name: Mirima National Park
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Kununurra and the DBCA Mirima page (both fetched) name it, Hidden Valley's banded sandstone 'mini Bungle Bungles' with 0.4-4 km walk trails 2 km from town.
objection: None of substance; a small park close to town, but clearly a visitor draw.

name: Kununurra Museum
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Kununurra only (fetched): local-history museum, Mon-Fri afternoons, donation entry.
objection: Small volunteer museum with weekday-afternoon hours and no second source; a 'only if you're nearby anyway' stop.

name: Kununurra Leisure Centre
reason: Rule 2: a local gym and public pool (amenity), not a visitor attraction.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it under Do; a hot-weather swim spot for travellers, but that holds for any town pool.

name: Ord Valley Muster
reason: Rule 4: a week-long annual festival in May, not a permanent place; belongs in Kununurra's best-time text.
objection: Well-known regional event; mention in the destination description.

name: Kununurra Race Club
reason: Rule 4: a venue that only matters on race and rodeo days in the dry season; otherwise nothing to see.
objection: Racing and rodeos are a genuine Kimberley experience, but they are events.

name: Wunaamin Miliwundi Ranges
reason: Rule 1 re-look: Australia's North West page for Wunaamin Miliwundi Ranges Conservation Park (fetched) and DBCA's Wunaamin park page name it; it holds Bell Gorge, Lennard River Gorge, Silent Grove campground and Mount Hart; a major Gibb River Road park.
objection: Its headline sights (Bell Gorge) are probably candidates in their own right; the park spot must not duplicate Bell Gorge. Name should be the park (Wunaamin Miliwundi Ranges Conservation Park / the 2023 split names Wunaamin and Miluwindi) - proposer to check.

name: Yarliyil Art Gallery
reason: Rule 1 re-look: Australia's North West blog '5 reasons to say Howdy to Halls Creek' (fetched) names Yarliyil Arts Gallery as the place to see local Aboriginal art; Shire of Halls Creek galleries page also lists it; rule 2: a gallery open to drop-in visitors.
objection: One counted source (a tourism-board blog post, not a listing) for an art centre whose primary role is selling art; marginal under the 'shop' exclusion, though Aboriginal art centres are a recognised visitor draw.

name: Five Rivers Lookout
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Wyndham, Tourism WA attraction page and Australia's North West listing (fetched) all name it; rule 2: summit of the Bastion Range over five rivers and Cambridge Gulf, a sunset picnic spot.
objection: Short visit; a drive-up lookout.

name: Big Crocodile, Wyndham
reason: Quirky roadside icon (COVERAGE include list): Wikivoyage Wyndham and Australia's North West Wyndham guide ('Big Croc', fetched) both name it; one of Australia's big things.
objection: A 15-minute photo stop; Wikivoyage: 'take a geeky photo and you're all done'. Name should be 'Big Crocodile' (no town in the name).

name: Afghan Cemetery, Wyndham
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Wyndham only (fetched): graves of 11 Afghan cameleers facing Mecca, with an unusual history.
objection: Rule 3: a small historic cemetery and a short look; only one counted source; may be a minor memorial.

name: Pioneer Cemetery, Wyndham
reason: Rule 3: minor historic cemetery; Wikivoyage gives it one line (12 meatworks graves) and no other visitor source singles it out; the 1,592 views are borrowed from an unrelated title.
objection: A heritage stop on a Wyndham history drive.

name: Wyndham Museum
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Wyndham and Australia's North West Wyndham guide (both fetched) name it, in the old courthouse with memorabilia and photos.
objection: Volunteer-run with erratic hours, open Apr-Oct 10-2 only; a short visit; may be closed when a visitor arrives (rule 2/4 risk).

name: Fisherman's Jetty, Wyndham
reason: Rule 3: a working fishing jetty given one line in Wikivoyage as a place to spot saltwater crocodiles; no second source and not a distinct draw.
objection: Croc-watching from the port is a real Wyndham experience; could go in Wyndham's or the port's bio.

name: MV Koolama
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Wyndham only (fetched): a 1942 wartime wreck in the mud 40 m from the wharf, with a gripping story.
objection: Visible only at low tide and only from the wharf; a ten-minute look with a single source.

name: Boab Prison Tree, Wyndham
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Wyndham and Visit Kununurra's 'Prison Tree' listing (the visitor centre, fetched) name it; a 2,000-year-old hollow boab used as the Hillgrove Lock-up, a quirky historic icon.
objection: King River Road is 4WD-only per Visit Kununurra; the tree is fenced and the prison story is partly folklore; short stop. Name should drop ', Wyndham' (keep it in wiki).

name: The Grotto, Wyndham
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Wyndham and Australia's North West Kununurra guide (both fetched) name it: a gorge reached by 140 steps with a swimming hole and wet-season waterfall.
objection: Small and mostly dry late in the season; a 30-60 minute stop. Name should be 'The Grotto' with the disambiguator in wiki.

name: Three Mile Valley
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Wyndham only (fetched): 'a pleasant hike beneath the Bastion Range'; one counted source with no detail.
objection: No distance, trail or managing agency named; possibly a local walk only. Needs a second source before it goes in.

name: Prison Boab Memorial Swimming Pool
reason: Rule 2: a town swimming pool (local amenity), not a visitor attraction.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it under Do.

name: Geikie Gorge
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Kimberley and DBCA Danggu Geikie Gorge National Park page (fetched: towering limestone walls, sandbank walk trail, freshwater crocodiles); a classic Kimberley gorge.
objection: Duplicate risk with a Danggu Geikie Gorge National Park candidate: they are one place; keep as one (name it Danggu Geikie Gorge, wiki Danggu Gorge National Park).

name: Prince Regent National Park
reason: Rule 1: DBCA page (fetched) promotes it as a bucket-list wilderness reached by boat or flight, with the Prince Regent River, King Cascade and terraced waterfalls; the cruise is the way in, the park is the place (COVERAGE 'A spot is a place').
objection: Only one counted source and no road access; a Dambimangari visitor pass is required; visited almost only on expensive coast cruises.

name: HMS Mermaid Boab Tree
reason: Rule 1: no counted source found; rule 3: a single inscribed tree at Careening Bay inside Prince Regent National Park, part of that larger spot.
objection: A real historic relic (1820) that Kimberley coast cruises land at; could be mentioned in Prince Regent National Park's bio.

name: Warlibirri National Park
reason: Rule 1: Wikipedia only; no DBCA visitor page (Explore Parks 404) or tourism source names it as somewhere to go.
objection: A gazetted national park; if DBCA later publishes a visitor page, re-judge.

name: Lawley River National Park
reason: Rule 1: Wikipedia only; no DBCA visitor page (404) or tourism source; no visitor access described.
objection: A gazetted park near Mitchell River NP; mainly seen from the air.

name: Niiwalarra Islands National Park
reason: Rule 1: Wikipedia only; no DBCA visitor page (404) or tourism listing; offshore islands with no visitor access described.
objection: Coast cruises pass the islands.

name: Bunuba National Park
reason: Rule 1: Wikipedia only; no DBCA visitor page found (404) and no tourism listing names it; its visitor sights are listed under their own names.
objection: A new park on Bunuba country in the central Kimberley; if it turns out to contain Windjana Gorge or Tunnel Creek, it may become a container for those spots.

name: Point Coulomb National Park
reason: Rule 1: Wikipedia only; no DBCA visitor page (404) or tourism source; no coordinates and no visitor facilities described.
objection: Coastal park on the Dampier Peninsula; Wikivoyage or DBCA may add it later.

name: Kimberley Marine Park
reason: Rule 2 and 3: a marine-park administrative zone along the whole coast, not a place a visitor goes to; its draws (Horizontal Falls, Montgomery Reef, King George Falls) are judged on their own.
objection: Real protected area; cruises operate within it.

name: Chinatown
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Broome (fetched) names Chinatown as the traditional retail strip along Carnarvon St; Broome's historic pearling-era quarter is a stop most visitors walk.
objection: Rule 2: Wikivoyage describes it as mainly shops and cafes ('don't expect gongs'); without a second source naming something to see (heritage buildings, Sun Pictures, pearl showrooms) it is a shopping strip. Name 'Chinatown' needs a wiki disambiguator.

name: One Arm Point
reason: Rule 1 re-look: Lonely Planet attraction 'Ardyaloon (One Arm Point)' and Visit Broome listing for the Ardyaloon Trochus Hatchery (fetched) name it as a Dampier Peninsula stop with hatchery tours and beaches.
objection: Several operators report the hatchery closed for repairs after cyclone damage; a community permit is needed; without the hatchery the draw is the views and crafts only.

name: Mount Elizabeth Station
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage Gibb River Road (fetched) and Australia's North West Gibb River Road page ('Mt Elizabeth Station Stay') name it; the base for Wunnamurra and Warla gorges.
objection: Brief: accommodation and stations are rejected as businesses; the gorges are the places and should be the spots if sources name them. Keep only if the station itself is treated as a destination base.

name: Home Valley Station
reason: Rule 1 re-look: Tourism Australia's Gibb River Road itinerary (fetched) uses Balanggarra Home Valley Station as a multi-night base 'where towering gorges meet waterfalls and billabongs', and Australia's North West lists it among the Gibb's main stops.
objection: It is a station resort (accommodation business); the gorges and Cockburn Range views it offers are the places, and none is named here as a spot.

name: Chamberlain Gorge
reason: Rule 1: Tourism WA attraction page (fetched) names Chamberlain Gorge in El Questro Wilderness Park; the gorge is the place the cruise goes to.
objection: Rule 3 and 2: inside El Questro Wilderness Park and seen only on the operator's boat cruise (May-Sep), so it may be part of an El Questro spot rather than distinct.

name: El Questro Gorge
reason: Rule 1 re-look: El Questro's own walking-trail guide (elquestro.com.au, the park's operator; fetched) describes the El Questro Gorge Trail to Halfway Pool and Micking Pool; travel press (Australian Geographic) names it a highlight.
objection: Rule 3: part of El Questro Wilderness Park; no Wikivoyage or Tourism WA listing found, and the operator's own document is the only counted source; Emma Gorge is the park's better-known gorge.

name: Broome
reason: Rule 1+2, town a guide gives its own section: Wikivoyage has a full Broome page (Sun Pictures, Cable Beach, pearl farms, camel rides); the Kimberley's main town and base, also a Tourism WA destination page.
objection: Destination-scale: the town itself may be a destination rather than a spot, and its draws (Cable Beach, Gantheaume Point) must not be duplicated as a town wrapper; that is the proposer's call, not an inclusion objection.

name: Derby
reason: Rule 1+2, town with its own guide section: Wikivoyage Derby page, 'best known for its giant prison Boab tree', with the long tidal jetty; a base at the west end of the Gibb River Road.
objection: Wikivoyage itself says you 'might stop off here' on the highway; if the Prison Boab Tree and jetty are listed as their own spots, the town may only be a wrapper (COVERAGE: a town is a spot only when the town itself is a draw).

name: Kununurra
reason: Rule 1+2, town visitors base in: Wikivoyage Kununurra page and a Tourism WA destination page; the east-Kimberley base for Lake Argyle, Mirima and Purnululu, with Lake Kununurra and Kelly's Knob in town.
objection: Mostly a base whose draws lie outside it; may be better as a destination than a spot (proposer's call).

name: Wyndham
reason: Rule 1+2, town with its own guide section: Wikivoyage Wyndham page has a See section (Five Rivers Lookout atop the Bastion Range, Fisherman's Jetty crocodiles, museum, giant croc statue).
objection: Small port; its headline (Five Rivers Lookout) could be listed as its own spot, leaving the town as a wrapper.

name: Warmun
reason: Rule 1: named twice by Wikivoyage (Kimberley region page and Kununurra 'Go next') as the Purnululu entry point with a long-standing Aboriginal art scene; the Warmun Art Centre is a recognised gallery.
objection: Only one-line mentions, no own guide section, and an Aboriginal community where the visitor draw is the art centre rather than the town: the Warmun Art Centre may be the right spot, or it is a gateway village whose draw is the journey beyond (Pipiriki benchmark -> review).

name: Camballin
reason: Rule 2: a town with nothing a source names to see; Wikivoyage gives one line ('has fishing on the Fitzroy River') and lists it only as a place the highway passes; no accommodation per source.
objection: It does appear in Wikivoyage's 'Other destinations' list, and river fishing is something to do; but that is a local use of a river, not a visitor draw.

name: Dampier Peninsula
reason: Rule 1+2: Tourism WA gives it its own destination page (Kimberley 'Explore More': Broome, Kununurra, Dampier Peninsula, Bungle Bungle Range) and Wikivoyage names it; beaches, Cape Leveque, Beagle Bay church and Aboriginal communities.
objection: A region-scale area rather than one place: its parts (Cape Leveque, Beagle Bay Sacred Heart Church) may be the spots and the peninsula a destination; risk of listing both.

name: Sun Pictures
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage Broome 'Do' listing; opened 1916, the world's oldest open-air cinema still operating, screening nightly, a recognised attraction rather than a plain venue.
objection: Wikivoyage notes it has 'lost some of its original atmosphere'; it is a working cinema, a venue whose use is watching a film (arguably a recurring show), though the venue is permanent and open nightly.

name: Broome Golf Club
reason: Rule 2/Leave out: a sports club; Wikivoyage mentions it only in passing, noting most visitors come just for a meal at the clubhouse, i.e. a restaurant.
objection: Drop-in golfers are welcome, so a visitor can play 18 holes; but a local golf course is not a distinct draw a traveller goes out of their way for.

name: El Questro Station
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage (Gibb River Road and Wyndham pages) lists El Questro Resort, Emma Gorge and El Questro Gorge; a 700,000-acre wilderness park open to visitors with a park pass, gorges and Zebedee thermal springs.
objection: It is a commercial station-resort (accommodation business); its real places are Emma Gorge, Zebedee Springs and El Questro Gorge, and if those are listed the station is a wrapper or a destination, not a spot.

name: Purnululu National Park
reason: Rule 1+2, obvious draw: DBCA park page and Wikivoyage Purnululu page; UNESCO World Heritage Bungle Bungle Range with gorge walks (Cathedral Gorge, Echidna Chasm) and campgrounds.
objection: Flagship national park, likely a destination rather than a spot (proposer's call); access is 4WD only and seasonal (closed in the Wet), which is a permanent venue that opens seasonally, so it still qualifies.

name: Bungle Bungle Range
reason: Rule 3 duplicate of Purnululu National Park: the range is the park's headline landform and the park is named for the place (COVERAGE: a park destination is named as the park); kept as one under Purnululu National Park.
objection: Tourism WA brands it 'Bungle Bungle Range' with its own page and it has more page views than the park, so the owner may prefer that name; either way only one of the two should ship.

name: Lake Argyle
reason: Rule 1+2: Wikivoyage Kununurra See listing (enormous lake, resort village, dam, picnic area, scenery) and the Kimberley page's lake beaches; Australia's second-largest artificial lake with cruises, swimming and the infinity pool.
objection: Visitors mostly see it on a cruise (an operator); but the lake itself is the place the cruise goes, so the lake is the spot.

name: Lake Kununurra Golf Club
reason: Rule 2/Leave out: a sports club; Wikivoyage lists it as a golf course, not an attraction a traveller goes out of their way for.
objection: Visitors can play the course by the lake; but a town golf course is a local amenity, not a distinct draw.

name: Kununurra Agricultural Show
reason: Rule 4: an event (two days in mid July per Wikivoyage's Events section), not a permanent place.
objection: None: events are never spots; it may go in a best-time text.

name: Wolfe Creek Crater
reason: Rule 1+2, obvious draw: DBCA park page (Wolfe Creek Meteorite Crater National Park: 400 m return walk to the rim, sunrise over the crater) and Wikivoyage park page; the world's second-largest crater with meteorite fragments.
objection: Remote, Tanami Road 4WD access, and a short visit (rim walk under an hour); the park and the crater are one place, so list only one.

name: Gwion Gwion Rock Paintings
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage's Kimberley page features them (image and art context); internationally known rock art with high page views.
objection: Not one place: an art style found at hundreds of remote sites, mostly reached on guided tours or flights (an operator), and the candidate has no coordinates; better listed as a named accessible site (e.g. on the Mitchell Falls walk or near Kalumburu) if a source names one, otherwise mentioned in a destination description.
